text:
Ravi: Heads up 1 Exec asked for a very tight observable MVP. We need to propose a single prioritized cut that balances customer asks and risk.

Anya: From customer interviews the top asks are: route cost breakdown, quick error triage (grouping + counts), and a way to flag cold starts in traces. They rank cost > errors > cold-start tracing.

Theo: Engineering reality: cost rollups are straightforward if we can get route tagging at ingress. Error grouping requires a cheap fingerprint algorithm and small retention. Cold-start tracing needs runtime hooks  and touches hot path unless we emit a tiny marker.

Megan: Legal: request sampling must avoid storing raw prompts for hosted customers. Dedicated customers can opt-in for deeper samples.

Ravi: Draft MVP suggestion: (A) per-route hourly rollups of tokens+requests+estimated cost, (B) error buckets with counts and link to sanitized example ids, (C) sampled traces with a single boolean cold_start tag (no expanded spans).

Anya: If we do that, rollout timeline looks like: infra + schema changes (2 sprints), backend rollups (1 sprint), frontend surface (1 sprint). Canary week to monitor CPU/token latency.

Theo: Implementation detail: add header X-Route-ID at proxy, enrich events with model_id and token_count, publish to obs-events topic. Rollup job pseudocode:
```
select route, date_hour, sum(tokens) as tokens, count(*) as reqs
from obs_events
group by route, date_hour
```
Store as materialized view for UI.

Megan: For error grouping use hashed signature: lower(prompt).remove_digits().truncate(256) -> sha256. That yields consistent buckets but legal still wants to avoid raw prompt retention. Only store signature + example_id.

Ravi: Launch criteria (short):
- Cost chart: per-route view + CSV export
- Error: top-20 buckets + count and link to one sanitized example id
- Traces: sampled <=3% with cold_start boolean and link from request detail
- No raw prompt storage for hosted customers

Anya: Risk register: storage spike for traces, privacy for examples, and perf regression. Mitigations: 3% sampling limit, 7-day retention for hosted traces, sanitization pipeline, and a runtime flag to drop tracing if backpressure.

Theo: Monitoring/Canary metrics: tokens_p50, tokens_p95, inference_cpu, trace_emit_failures. We should auto-disable tracing if trace_emit_failures > 0.5% in canary.

Megan: Pilot customers (NoteWave, SigmaHealth) ok to join for dedicated repros later. I'll coordinate opt-in contracts.

Ravi: If exec forces cuts: cut CSV export and extend trace retention to 0 days (i.e., only link to ephemeral example ids) to save storage.

ci-bot: RFC created: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/obs-prio-1777  add owners.

Anya: One nit  please avoid "repro prompt" language in public docs. Use "sanitized example id".

Theo: Agree. Also will prototype a cold_start microspan that is just a JSON flag to minimize payload.

Ravi: OK final: we'll present this MVP and rollout plan at 4pm. I'll update the roadmap doc and add the canary checklist. Any blockers?

Megan: Legal signoff pending on sanitized example retention policy. I'll escalate.

Anya: No other blockers from PM side.
